summary: ionic-insta-api-wrapper exfiltrates Instagram credentials and session data to author-controlled backend
details: The package's getCookie() helper performs Instagram login and then unconditionally POSTs the Instagram username, plaintext password, the full login request body, and the full login response (including session data) to the hardcoded author-controlled endpoint https://reelsaver.appit-online.de/v2/insta/check. The destination is not Instagram and is not caller-configurable on this path. After login/2FA, LoginService.verifyAccount() fetches a user/post list from https://reelsaver.appit-online.de/v2/insta/verify and automatically invokes follow() and like() against the returned targets using the just-obtained Instagram authorization, covertly driving the installer's authenticated end-user session to boost attacker-chosen accounts and posts. Additionally, InstaService.fetchAPI() emits a per-call GET to https://reelsaver.appit-online.de/v2/insta/<userId>/<target>/<type>, leaking the logged-in username and every lookup target to the same backend. Any application built on this wrapper will relay its end-users' Instagram credentials, session artifacts, and browsing graph to the author, while also performing author-directed social actions on those users' accounts.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
